newsitem.title: USA: CalPERS to reorganise domestic equity management.
newsitem.headline: CalPERS to reorganise domestic equity management.

text.p: The California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) said it had voted to reorganize the management of its domestic equity portfolio in order to enhance fund returns.

The plan included developing an internal capability to manage a part of the fund's domestic equity in-house, streamlining the external manager contracts solicitation process, and revamping the pay-for-performance fee schedule for external managers, CalPERS said.

"We're maintaining our passive portfolios as a sound foundation, seeking aggressive equity managers, and adding a specialized investment portfolio to control risk in an effort to open doors to new opportunities for the fund," said Charles Valdes, chair of CalPERS Investment Committee.
Roughly 84 percent, or $39.3 billion, of the fund's domestic equity assets were now passively managed internally, it said.
Under the new structure, active management of domestic equities could increase to 20 percent, it said.
